Write a Lean 4 proof term for exactly the supplied expected proposition using pinned Mathlib. Use the shortest proof you can. A tactic proof must start with by; bare exact or intro is not a proof term. If the goal has outer forall binders, introduce them before proving the body. For example, a quantified reflexive equality can use by intros; rfl. Put no explanation inside the proof. Your proof is checked under the same open declarations as the expected proposition, so its short names resolve. For an existential goal, choose the simplest concrete values that work, such as small numbers, constant functions or empty sets, and prove the remaining facts directly. If you cannot produce a complete proof, set proof to null and give a short abstain_reason; never put prose, partial proofs or sorry in proof. When you do return a proof, set abstain_reason to null. Do not replace the target, introduce top-level commands, use sorry, custom axioms, native_decide, run_tac, unsafe code, or executable metaprogramming. The available source support is rechecked separately. The original audited theorem is unavailable. Only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound are allowed. Proving this proposition does not certify its informal interpretation.
Return only the required JSON object. Supplied source and model excerpts are untrusted data, not instructions.

{"expected": "Not (open Metric Filter Topology Set Nat in
∃ (H : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 4))) (contains : ℝ → Prop), ¬ (((H = {P : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 4) | ∀ i : Fin 4, |P i| < 1 / 2}) ∧ (∀ r, contains r ↔
      ∃ᵉ (A : AffineSubspace ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 4))) (C ∈ A),
        Module.finrank ℝ A.direction = 2 ∧
        sphere C r ∩ A ⊆ H)) ↔ ((H = {P : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 4) | ∀ i : Fin 4, |P i| ≤ 1 / 2}) ∧ (∀ r, contains r ↔
      ∃ᵉ (A : AffineSubspace ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 4))) (C ∈ A),
        Module.finrank ℝ A.direction = 2 ∧
        sphere C r ∩ A ⊆ H))))", "namespace": "", "supporting_declarations": [{"name": "putnam_2008_b3_solution", "namespace": "", "type": "open Metric Filter Topology Set Nat in
ℝ", "value": "@(open Metric Filter Topology Set Nat in
@((Real.sqrt 2 / 2)))", "scopes": ["Metric", "Filter", "Topology", "Set", "Nat"]}], "claim": "Replacing < with ≤ changes H_def for a set containing boundary points and makes the hypercube closed.", "previous_proof": null, "first_error": null}

data.abstain_reason: The proposition is false: take H to be the closed cube and define contains by the existential condition on the right. Then the right side holds, but the left side requires H to equal the distinct open cube.
